name: Deep moisture and protein
tagline: A guide to conditioning hair that is dry, rough or breaking.
image_alt: A woman with long cornrow braids and defined baby hair, in profile.
description: Why hair feels dry or rough, an eight-week conditioning routine, when protein and bond treatments are worth using, and what to look for on a label.
intro: Condition consistently. Use the stronger treatments on purpose, not whenever hair feels dry. Then change what you do based on how your hair answers.

causes.title: Why hair feels dry, rough or stiff
causes.intro: Hair can feel the same way for several different reasons, which is why swapping products at random rarely fixes it.
items: A harsh cleanser, or washing more often than your hair needs.
It takes the oils with the buildup, and the hair has nothing left on it.
Skipping the deep conditioner, or rinsing the leave-in out.
Conditioning is what puts slip back. Without it, every comb-through costs you hair.
Layers of styler, oil and dry shampoo that never quite come off.
Hair can feel coated and limp, and nothing new seems to work on it.
They change the hair fiber itself, and that damage does not wash out.
Detangling dry, brushing hard, tight styles, pulling through knots.
Most breakage is mechanical. It happens in your hands, not in the bottle.
Protein, bond and lipid treatments all in the same week.
If three things change together, you cannot tell which one helped and which one made hair stiff.

stock.title: Before you start
stock.intro: Write these down today, with photos. Check the same list at week 4 and week 8.
items: How long after washing does your hair start to feel dry?
Where does it tangle most? Ends, underneath, the crown?
Which areas break: ends, mid-lengths, crown, sides, or all over.
How hard it is to detangle and style, and how soft it feels.
Strand thickness, how dense it is, your curl pattern.
What you have had done, and how recently.
Cleanser, conditioner, deep conditioner, leave-in, oils, treatments.
Recent protein or bond treatments, and what your hair did afterwards.

routine.title: Your routine
routine.intro: One wash day a week. The treatment step is the only part that changes from week to week.

wash.title: Your wash day
steps: Wash the scalp gently and rinse it all the way out.
Protein, lipid or bond, if this week calls for one. Follow its own label for how long to leave it on and how to rinse it. Only one treatment per wash day.
Deep conditioner on wash day, or your usual rinse-out.
With the conditioner still in, and enough slip to get through. Then rinse.
Style with as little pulling and handling as you can.
What you used, and how your hair felt afterwards. This is the part that makes week 8 worth anything.

between.title: Between wash days
groups: Leave it alone where you can. Less combing, less restyling.
Refresh only with something that adds slip, not buildup.
Keep styles comfortable and low tension.
Protect your hair from friction. Silk or satin.
Do not sleep in anything tightly secured.
Check whether your ends need something.
Note anything that changed after a treatment.

ing.title: What to look for on a conditioning label
ing.intro: These show up in conditioners, masks, leave-ins and treatments. The ingredient list on the back is what tells you which job a product is really set up to do.
items: They attract water and hold on to it. How well that works depends on the formula and the weather.
Conditions the hair and improves how it feels.
The slip in a good conditioner. Less friction through a comb means less breakage.
Fatty alcohols. They thicken conditioners and soften hair. Not the drying kind of alcohol.
Lipids like the ones hair loses to washing and heat. The idea is well supported; how much any one product does varies.
Lubrication and softness. They sit on the surface and cut friction.
Keratin, wheat, rice or silk. They cling to damaged spots and temporarily improve how hair behaves. That is not the same as rebuilding it.
Several different technologies, each targeting different damage. Judge the product, not the category.

trouble.title: If something feels off
items: Look at your cleanser first, then whether the leave-in and styler are sealing anything in.
Look at slip, how you detangle, and what your hair rubs against all day.
Look at handling, heat and what you have had done, before you buy a treatment.
Buildup, or too many products layered. Clarify, then simplify.
Reduce it or stop it, and reassess. Do not repeat it automatically.
Product buildup, or too much conditioning. Not a reason to add protein.
Look at surface conditioning, heat and general wear.

end.title: At the end of eight weeks
notes: Compare your week 8 notes and photos with your baseline. Keep the cleansing, conditioning, deep conditioning and leave-in. Keep lipid support at an interval you will actually stick to. Keep protein and bond treatments only if your hair clearly answered them.
list: How much of the routine you actually kept up

timeline.title: Your eight weeks
timeline.intro: One wash day a week. The conditioning stays the same all the way through, and only the treatment changes. Swipe through to see what each week is for.

kit.label: Your every-wash-day kit
use: Heat protectant, if you use heat

items.title: Deep conditioning
items.text: Your baseline. Plain, steady conditioning first, so you can see how your hair does on its own.

items.title: Lipid support
items.text: Bring in your ceramide or lipid product. Notice whether your hair feels smoother, softer, coated, or no different.

items.title: Protein, or not
items.text: Only if your hair has asked for it. This week is a decision, not an instruction.
notes: you have color, bleach, relaxer or regular heat in your history, you're seeing breakage, and protein has suited you before.
little chemical or heat history and no clear breakage. Use the week for conditioning instead. You're not missing anything.
stiff, rough or hard to detangle afterwards? Don't repeat it. Go back to your moisturizing conditioner, then look at buildup and handling.

items.title: Evaluate
items.text: Back to moisture. Take your week 4 photos and compare them with your baseline.
notes: stiff, limp, rough or coated hair all have several possible causes, and you can't diagnose protein overload by touch. Treat what you notice as clues, not a diagnosis.

items.title: Bond support
items.text: For hair with color, bleach, relaxer or heat in its history. Follow the product's directions exactly.

items.title: Lipid support again
items.text: Same as week 2. Take a look at buildup and how many products you're layering.

items.title: Protein check
items.text: Only if week 3 went well and your hair still seems to want it.
notes: hair that doesn't need protein doesn't benefit from it, and can end up stiff. If in doubt, condition.

items.title: Consolidate
items.text: Final wash, final photos. Build your everyday routine out of whatever worked, and let go of whatever didn't.
